title: I. Man's principle is God; Gen 1:26-27; Acts 17; theology must know God
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): I. Ye principle belonging toward man is God. For from God man was created Genesis 1:26-27. But since man from God is, plus from Him according to theological consideration most nearly depends, this place is proper where concerning God it is treated. Ye theologian cannot man unto God his king plus principle lead back unless GOD known he has. Hence ye Apostle Acts 17 proclaims God ye creator; now commands all that they repent because He appointed a day belonging toward judgment through Christ from ye dead raised.
pass_b_english: I. The principle of man is God. For man was created by God (Genesis 1:26-27).

But since man is from God and depends on Him most nearly according to theological consideration, this is the proper place to treat of God. For the theologian cannot lead man back to God his King and principle, and onward to eternal life, unless he has God known.
Hence the Apostle too (Acts 17:24-31) proclaims God the creator; and now commands all everywhere to repent, because He has appointed a day of judgment through Christ raised from the dead.
source_text: I. Principium hominis est Deus. Nam a Deo homo conditus est Gen. 1.26-27. Quoniam vero homo a Deo est, & ab eo secundum considerationem Theologicam proxime dependet, hic locus proprius est, ubi de Deo agatur. Jam vero hominem ad Deum, regem & principium suum reducere & ad vitam aeternam deducere non potest Theologus, nisi DEUM cognitum habeat. Hinc & Apostolus Act. 17.24-31 Deum creatorem praedicat; nunc mandat omnibus ut resipiscant, eo quod statuit diem judicii per Christum a mortuis suscitatum.
